summary: Iteration 3 (Stripe subscriptions + plan-based limits + Powered-by branding) fully verified. Backend: 14/14 new pytest tests PASSED — /plans (Free 0 / Pro 29 pro_monthly / Business 79 business_monthly), /payments/checkout returns valid Stripe checkout_url + cs_ session_id and creates a payment_transactions record (initiated/pending, plan=pro); invalid lookup_key -> 400; unauthenticated checkout -> 401/403; /payments/status/{session_id} public (returns session_id/status/payment_status/plan, unknown id -> 404); FREE user (fresh register + completed onboarding = 1 collection) cannot create a 2nd collection (402 with upgrade message) and cannot create a 2nd widget after creating the first (402); admin (pro) can freely create multiple collections and widgets with no 402; /public/widget/{id} for the free workspace's widget returns branding:true and for the admin (pro) workspace widget returns branding:false; regression /public/collection/testify-demo/submit still returns ok:true and /public/wall/testify-demo returns branding:false (admin pro). Frontend E2E (most important, fully automated): registered a fresh random-email user, completed Onboarding wizard (business name -> color -> collection name -> Finish -> Go to dashboard), went to Dashboard -> Settings -> Plans & billing card (testid=billing) shows current-free, clicked upgrade-pro, was redirected to https://checkout.stripe.com hosted page showing 'Subscribe to Testify Pro US$29.00 / month' in Sandbox mode. Filled email, card 4242 4242 4242 4242 exp 12/34 cvc 123, cardholder name, US address (1 Market St, San Francisco, 94105, CA), and PHONE (Stripe now requires it — see note below). Clicked Subscribe -> Stripe redirected back to /payment/success?session_id=cs_test_... which polled /api/payments/status and rendered 'Welcome to Pro! 🎉' (data-testid payment-success) plus 'Go to dashboard' button (data-testid go-dashboard). Re-opened /dashboard/settings -> Billing now says 'You're currently on the Pro plan' AND data-testid current-pro is visible. Verified upgrade unlocks limit: POST /api/collections with the same JWT succeeded (200) creating a 2nd collection — no more 402.

minor.issue: Collection creation inside onboarding uses unique_slug(...) but is not wrapped in DuplicateKeyError retry — when two fresh users onboard concurrently with identical collection_name the second returns 500 (reproduced by pytest-xdist LoadScope running fresh_user fixture twice in parallel; serial run passed 14/14). Same class of bug as previously flagged for _create_default_workspace.

ui_bugs.issue: After successful register the code calls navigate('/onboarding') but the ProtectedRoute / AuthContext race lands the user on /dashboard instead — the onboarding wizard is skipped and workspace has no default collection until the user manually visits /onboarding. Reproduced twice: URL after submit was /dashboard with an empty Overview and no collections. Working around by explicit page.goto('/onboarding') completes onboarding correctly.

action_items: Fix Register.jsx → Onboarding navigation: user is auto-redirected to /dashboard instead of /onboarding after register. Likely a ProtectedRoute/AuthContext state race — recommend awaiting refreshUser() before navigate('/onboarding'), or guarding /dashboard route to redirect to /onboarding while user.onboarded === false.
Wrap the onboarding first-collection insert in a DuplicateKeyError retry (same pattern already used in _create_default_workspace) to eliminate 500s under concurrent onboarding.

Stripe Checkout now requires a phone number on this account (red-highlighted field blocks 'Subscribe'). Not a bug per se, but the in-UI hint text mentions only card/expiry/CVC — consider updating the hint under Billing.jsx (line 54) or documenting.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py continues to grow past 1100 lines — routers for payments and public endpoints should be split out.

/payments/status returns cached DB status without re-polling Stripe once payment_status is already 'paid' — fine, but there's no rate-limit / auth on this public endpoint so anyone with a session id can enumerate. Consider requiring the session id belong to the caller when a JWT is present, or add basic rate limiting.

_apply_paid does not verify the payment_transactions row is already paid before flipping the workspace plan on webhook — if a duplicate/late webhook arrives for a subsequently downgraded workspace it will re-upgrade. Add an idempotency guard using status==completed before workspace update.

Billing.jsx does not show any receipt / subscription id / cancel-subscription UI after upgrade — current-pro is disabled but users cannot cancel. Consider a 'Manage subscription' link to Stripe billing portal.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows including full Stripe hosted checkout automation
